items.defect: BOUND TESTS contradicts requirement 10 (past-cap windows). Requirement 10 says windows past MAX_TURNS are emitted as STUBS `{index, stub:true, complete:false}`, and requirement 16 pins `index` as "the window's 0-based position in turns[]", so stubs live in turns[]. The acceptance criterion then asserts, for a 500-turn synthetic session, BOTH `turns.length === 400` AND "every past-cap window present as {index, stub:true, complete:false} — asserted by key set, not by absence". If windows 400..499 are present, turns.length is 500, not 400. The two cannot both hold. This is the exact defect class the revision was written to remove (it is blocker #4's 'mutually unsatisfiable criteria' reappearing at the MAX_TURNS boundary that requirement 10 introduced), and it is unrecoverable by guessing: an agent that satisfies the length assertion drops the stubs and reinstates the inverted-bias trap requirement 10 exists to close.
items.requiredFix: Rewrite the criterion to the shape requirement 10 actually specifies, and state what MAX_TURNS counts (boundary windows, not records). E.g.: a session with 500 turn boundaries yields turns.length === 500, turns.filter(t => !t.stub).length === 400, entry.truncatedAtTurn === 400, and turns[400..499] each deepEqual {index:n, stub:true, complete:false}. If instead stubs are meant to live outside turns[], say which array holds them and restate requirement 16's index rule accordingly.

items.defect: isTurnBoundary keys the slash-command branch on the wrong tag, so on real data slash commands open no window at all — while the acceptance fixture is built to a record shape that barely occurs, making the test green over a dead feature. Requirement 7: a boundary is "an envelope whose opening tag is 'command-name' (kind 'command')". Measured over 300 real session files under ~/.claude/projects on this machine (757 string user turns): opening tag `command-message` = 43, `command-name` = 6, `local-command-caveat` = 6, `local-command-stdout` = 6, `task-notification` = 109, `scheduled-task` = 11, `system-reminder` = 3, `cross-session-message` = 1. The repo's OWN committed fixture is the same shape: test/fixtures/claude-projects/proj-automated/sessE.jsonl content is "<command-message>honestweek is running</command-message>\n<command-name>/honestweek</command-name>". `command-message` is in MACHINE_ENVELOPE_TAGS, so ~88% of real slash-command turns classify as machine, open no window, produce no sidecar row, and their tool_uses carry turn:null and are dropped from window attribution. Meanwhile the acceptance criteria ("MACHINE ENVELOPES OPEN NO WINDOW" and "SLASH-COMMAND ARGS NEVER READ") both use a synthetic '<command-name>run-tests</command-name><command-args>SECRETARG</command-args>' record, so both pass while the branch they claim to prove never fires on a real log.
items.requiredFix: Define the command branch by CONTENT, not by opening tag: a user string record that is machine-envelope-only is a boundary of kind 'command' iff it contains a well-formed <command-name>…</command-name> block; the window's instruction text is that block's inner text (still never <command-args>, never <command-message>). Restate requirement 7 and requirement 12 in those terms, and require at least one acceptance fixture whose record is byte-shaped like sessE.jsonl (<command-message> first, then <command-name>, then <command-args>) asserting exactly one window of kind 'command' with the command-name text as its instruction.

items.defect: The load-bearing structural privacy control is unsatisfiable against two other requirements, so an implementer must weaken the one criterion the spec says must not be weakened. "NO PROSE IN THE DRAFT" asserts "every turns[] and ideas[] object has exactly the specified key set and every string value is either a member of a closed vocabulary (a cue, 'prose'|'command', 'you'|'assistant', a tool name, a status token) or matches /^[0-9a-f]{8}$/". (i) Requirement 20 puts commitShas[]/inspectedShas[] on every window, and extractCommits (claude-adapter.mjs:300-304) harvests /[0-9a-f]{7,40}/ — a 7-char short SHA and a 40-char rev-parse SHA both fail /^[0-9a-f]{8}$/. The "SHA CAUSE SPLIT" criterion REQUIRES a fixture window with non-empty commitShas, so the two criteria cannot both pass. (ii) Requirement 10's stub windows carry exactly 3 keys, not the 14-key set, so "exactly the specified key set" is false for every stub. Because this is the assertion the promptVerbatim probe would have failed, an unconstrained loosening of it is precisely the failure mode the revision is meant to prevent.
items.requiredFix: State the scan as a per-shape whitelist: (a) stub windows must deepEqual {index:number, stub:true, complete:false}; (b) non-stub windows must have exactly the 14 specified keys; (c) string values must match their key: ref/shapeKey /^[0-9a-f]{8}$/, kind in ['prose','command'], correctionObserved in ['yes','no','unknown'], statusSignals/testSignals in the deriveStatus token set ['pass','fail','build-broke'], commitShas/inspectedShas /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/ ONLY, toolsUsed keys tool-name-shaped with number values; ideas exactly {turn,ref,origin,cue} with origin in ['you','assistant'] and cue in IDEA_CUES. No catch-all 'or 8-hex' clause.

items.defect: MAX_IDEAS is enumerated as a window-local bound but is session-scoped, so it reintroduces (in miniature) the structural bias requirement 9's enumeration exists to remove. Requirement 9 justifies the complete=false list as "the WINDOW-LOCAL evidence bounds", but requirement 19 pushes ideas into the session-scoped acc.ideas under one shared MAX_IDEAS = 40 (the same shape as MAX_STEERS = 60, which requirement 9 correctly excludes). Once the 41st idea in a session is dropped, every later window that would have produced an idea is marked complete === false and becomes ungradeable for the rest of the session — the same 'a cap bites once and poisons the tail' effect that made blocker #4's criteria unsatisfiable. No acceptance criterion tests it: the 100-human-turn criterion only exercises MAX_STEERS, and its fixture need contain no idea cues.
items.requiredFix: Either (a) make ideas window-local (MAX_IDEAS_PER_TURN, counted per open window, and keep the session array capped separately WITHOUT touching the flag), or (b) move MAX_IDEAS to the 'does NOT touch the flag' list with the same rationale given for MAX_STEERS/MAX_NOTES. Whichever is chosen, add an acceptance criterion: a synthetic session that trips MAX_IDEAS asserts the expected complete value on windows after the cap bites.

items.defect: Two load-bearing acceptance criteria compare against a 'pre-change value' that no requirement tells the agent to create. "DRAFT SUPERSET" requires every pre-existing draft key to be assert.deepEqual to "its pre-change value", and the third "REDACTION ORDER FIX" assertion requires discover over the fixture corpus to be "byte-identical before and after the reorder". A test run after the change has no access to the before state; both need a committed baseline snapshot of the pre-change draft. No requirement creates one, filesTouched lists no such file, and the golden harness covers built output only (Layer 1), not the draft (Layer 2). Since Layer 2 has no byte-identity gate, these two ARE the substitute gate — an agent that improvises (e.g. asserting shape rather than value, or regenerating the baseline after the change) silently disables it.
items.requiredFix: Add a requirement to commit a baseline artifact generated from the CURRENT HEAD before any code change — e.g. test/fixtures/golden/draft-pre-phase1.json produced by running discover over test/fixtures/claude-projects with a fixed week and redactor — add it to filesTouched, and restate both criteria as deepEqual/byte-compare against that committed file. Note explicitly that the baseline is generated pre-change and must not be regenerated afterwards.

items.defect: MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES = 8 MiB is declared but its enforcement behaviour is never specified and nothing tests it. Requirement 8 declares the constant; requirement 22 says discover prints "any MAX_PROMPT_LEN / MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES cap hits" as counts; cross-cutting P2 says "exceeding either is reported as a count on stdout". Nothing says what happens to the data: stop pushing rows, drop the largest rows, truncate the file, or write it oversized and merely warn. The "SIDECAR BOUNDS" acceptance criterion exercises MAX_PROMPT_LEN only. Two agents will implement two different behaviours on the highest-leak-density file in the system, and neither is falsifiable by the criteria as written.
items.requiredFix: Specify the rule (recommended: rows are appended in stream order and pushing stops once the serialized budget would be exceeded; the sidecar is still written, and the count of dropped rows is printed), and add an acceptance criterion: a synthetic corpus exceeding MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES yields a sidecar under the budget, a dropped-row count on stdout, and a still-valid JSON document.

items.defect: The promptSink contract is under-specified in two places an agent must guess. (i) Requirement 20 says adaptOneSession "pushes {ref, sessionId, turn, text} per window opening and {ref, sessionId, turn, origin, cue, text} per idea" — into a single array (discover then discriminating rows by the presence of `cue`) or into an object {prompts:[], ideas:[]}? The sidecar shape in cross-cutting P2 has two separate arrays, so the mapping is inferable but not stated. (ii) refFor(sessionId, turnIndex, origin, redactedText) takes an `origin`, and the test plan asserts refFor is origin-sensitive, but a window-opening prompt row has no origin defined (ideas do). An agent must guess 'you' — and a wrong guess silently breaks ref equality between a window and its own prompt row, which is the join key Phase 3's carry depends on.
items.requiredFix: State the sink as `promptSink = { prompts: [], ideas: [] }` (or an array plus an explicit discriminator field), and state that a window-opening row uses origin 'you' — the same value refFor receives for a human-side idea — with an acceptance assertion that a window's `ref` equals its sidecar row's `ref`.

items.defect: Requirement 33 instructs adding a README '## Sidecars' row that already exists, and two line references drift. README.md:266 already carries the honestweek.harvest.json row ("Proposed redaction-denylist candidates from `harvest`. **Gitignored.**"), so "gains ... a honestweek.harvest.json row" risks a duplicate table row. Separately, the sidecar-table assertion cited as test/docs.test.mjs:96-100 is actually at test/docs.test.mjs:91-95 (line 96-100 is the sample-output test), and README.md:83 says "tagged claims, reversals, and cited commits" rather than the "cited SHAs" wording the requirement quotes (SKILL.md:25 does say SHAs). All other line refs I spot-checked are exact (claude-adapter.mjs:50-56/133-141/263/268/300-304/308-309/321-333/344-346/352-356/370-372/381/388/457-471/490-518/529; handoffs.mjs:18-21/30-31/85/136-137/144; discover.mjs:53-70/92/119/155-157/160; harvest.mjs:55-65/74-84/105-113/149-153; init.mjs:21/150; redact.test.mjs:19; claude-adapter.test.mjs:40/59/84; discover.test.mjs:34/125; handoffs.test.mjs:19; refuses-to-lie.test.mjs:140-141; config.mjs:29; README.md:246 and SKILL.md:31 both do omit `page`), and `node --test` does pass 371/371 at HEAD.
items.requiredFix: Change requirement 33 to 'add the honestweek.prompts.json row; the honestweek.harvest.json row already exists at README.md:266 — leave it', and correct the two line references.

items.defect: The '279 vs 281' acceptance numbers are construction-dependent and the source string is not given. I reproduced the direction and the mechanism against the real modules — redact('/home/alice/notes') is '[redacted:path]' (17 chars -> 15, net -2), so old order = 280-char slice + ellipsis - 2 and new order = 281 — but a plausible 358-char string with the path at offset 40 gave me 278, not 279, because truncate() trimEnd()s the slice and my cut landed on a space. (My first attempt gave 55/55 because filler runs of >=32 word chars hit OPAQUE_RE.) The 303-char email case reproduces exactly as claimed: old order emits 'alice@corp-…' (contains '@', not 'corp-secret'), new order emits '[redacted:e…'.
items.requiredFix: Either give the exact fixture string in the criterion, or restate it as a relation rather than two magic numbers: newLength === oldLength + 2, with the cut position asserted not to fall on whitespace. Also note in the criterion that filler must not contain a 32+ character word-run, or OPAQUE_RE dominates the measurement.

items.defect: The whole P5 unconfigured-noun gate hangs on `config.redaction.strictLaneNouns` (phase-2 requirements 12 and 14/rule 10, and the UNCONFIGURED-NOUN CHECK acceptance criterion), but lib/config.mjs:156-160 rebuilds `redaction` as exactly `{ codenames, names, terms }` from the raw JSON and silently DROPS every other key — it does not even fail loud, because the only `fail()` on that path fires when `redaction` is not an object. lib/config.mjs appears in no phase's filesTouched (phase-1 or phase-2). So a user who sets `"strictLaneNouns": true` gets `config.redaction.strictLaneNouns === undefined` at runValidate/runBuild time (both go through loadConfig), the noun check stays a warning forever, and the acceptance criterion 'the same input with strictLaneNouns true exits 2 with no output file' cannot pass as written. This is the same silent fail-open shape the spec correctly treats as blocker-severity for the copy gate.
items.requiredFix: Add /path/to/your/repo/lib/config.mjs to phase 2's filesTouched and add an explicit requirement: normalize `redaction.strictLaneNouns` as an optional boolean beside codenames/names/terms (defaulting false), failing loud on a non-boolean, exactly as `voice.denyMeta` is handled at config.mjs:227-238. Add test/config.test.mjs to filesTouched with an assertion that the flag survives loadConfig, and state that the strict half of the UNCONFIGURED-NOUN criterion drives the build through a real on-disk config file.

items.defect: The phase mandates a rendered self-contradiction. Requirement 18 says lane rows must NOT increment report.mjs's `total`, 'so a week with only lane rows must still print the honest "no interactive coding sessions" line', and the test plan asserts it. digest.mjs:49 and report.mjs:47 both emit `_No interactive coding sessions were found for this week._`. But a technique band can only render when build's re-derivation found interactive sessions (requirement 12 aborts exit 2 when the session-log root yields zero files, and every receipt must resolve to a window in one of those sessions). So the artifact states that no interactive coding sessions were found, directly above a band derived from them. This is exactly the Layer-6 defect class the revision fixed for digest.mjs:25, page.mjs:391 and README.md:127 — the fourth instance was missed.
items.requiredFix: Add this string to requirement 20's conditional-scoping list: when a lane band renders, digest.mjs:48-50 and report.mjs:46-48 must emit a scoped variant (e.g. '_No distilled work items for this week; the transcript-derived bands below are all that was measured._') and the current literal byte-for-byte otherwise. Add an acceptance criterion asserting the unscoped literal does NOT appear in any output that also carries a lane row, and that page.mjs:369's empty-feed literal gets the same treatment.

items.defect: The new fixtures and the golden harness collide, and the spec never says which wins. The test plan requires 'New fixtures under new project dirs in test/fixtures/claude-projects', while acceptance criteria 1, 4 and 5 require byte-identity against PHASE 1's committed goldens for all six modes / the archive snapshot / page mode. That fixture tree is the hermetic harness's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR root (phase-1 acceptance criterion 2). Session-derived numbers read it: page.mjs:128 computes per-group activeDays from `sessions.days[].byProject[label]`, and lib/site/sessions.mjs:233 reports `filesFound: files.length` over the whole root into the site bundle. The new grading fixtures must map to a configured non-display repo or adaptOneSession makes them private (claude-adapter.mjs:487-490) and they produce no windows at all — so they necessarily enter the same root the goldens are a function of. Acceptance criterion 3 compounds this by requiring site-mode 'byte-identical' output without naming a baseline (Phase 1's golden file, or the same build with the key omitted?).
items.requiredFix: State explicitly either (a) the lane fixtures live under a SECOND fixture root used only by lane tests, and the golden harness keeps Phase 1's root untouched — in which case acceptance criterion 3's site case must build against that second root and compare against a same-run lane-free build, not against Phase 1's golden; or (b) the goldens are regenerated in this phase, in which case acceptance criteria 1/4/5 must be restated as 'page/site goldens are regenerated in this commit and the diff is confined to session-derived counts', since byte-identity against a regenerated golden asserts nothing. Name the baseline for every byte-identity criterion in the phase.

items.defect: Requirement 14's rule 8 ('repeat the display-repo and configured-private-term checks (:114-127) for technique text — they are NOT inherited') cannot be repeated as written. validate.mjs:96-97 computes `isDisplay` from `itemRepoLabel(item)`, i.e. `item.repo ?? item.repoLabel ?? item.label` — a FIELD, not the text. Requirement 9 defines the technique shape as `{ id, text, receipt }` with no repo field, so the display half of rule 8 is structurally a no-op and an implementer must invent a text-scan check the spec never specifies. The gap is substantive, not cosmetic: a display-role repo LABEL in technique prose is caught by nothing else either, because excludeSet(config) (harvest.mjs:80-82) adds every repo label to the P5 exclusions, and the configured-private-term check only reads redaction.codenames/names/terms.
items.requiredFix: Specify the technique-side display check literally as a TEXT check that does not exist today: a technique whose normalized `text` contains the label of any config.repos entry with role 'display' is a validate problem and a build abort, reported by id and never echoed. Say whether featured/reference labels in technique text are permitted (they are, for work items). Add the matching acceptance criterion and an explicit note that this is a new rule, not a repeat of validate.mjs:114-120.

items.defect: The zero-corpus abort has no named mechanism, and build's adaptSessions call names arguments build does not have. Requirement 12 aborts when 'the session-log root yields ZERO files', citing warnIfNoSessionLogs (build.mjs:119) — but that reads `sessions.filesFound` from deriveSessions, and requirement 11 routes the lane through `adaptSessions`, which returns a bare entries array (claude-adapter.mjs:529-546) and which phase-1 requirement 26 explicitly forbids changing ('STILL RETURNS THE ENTRIES ARRAY, unchanged'). The natural implementation (`entries.length === 0`) is a different predicate than 'zero files'. Requirement 11 also lists `projectsRoot` in the call's option bag, but build has no projectsRoot (build.mjs:113-117 states as an invariant that neither the site nor page path passes one), and it lists `weekStart, weekEnd` while build's `week` is string-shaped at that point (build.mjs:253) — the Date reconstruction only exists inside the page branch at :378-379.
items.requiredFix: Name the symbol: build calls the already-exported `enumerateSessionFiles(resolveProjectsRoot())` (claude-adapter.mjs:71 / :65) and aborts on `length === 0`, separately from the entries result. State that build passes NO projectsRoot (so CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR remains the single override, keeping the harness hermetic) and that it constructs `weekStart`/`weekEnd` Dates from `week.start`/`week.end` exactly as build.mjs:378-379 does, hoisted above the gate.

items.defect: The 'COMMAND WINDOWS AND FILLER YIELD NOTHING' criterion ends 'a corpus mixing repeated CLI boilerplate openings with one genuine repeated instruction yields exactly one "held up"', but requirement 6 says 'Every eligible window in a qualifying shapeKey group carries "held up"'. A genuine instruction repeated across two sessions is two windows, so gradeTurns' map contains TWO 'held up' entries and one group; the deduplication to one ROW happens later, in build. The criterion never says whether it counts grades, groups or rendered rows, so a literal test of gradeTurns' output fails against the requirement that produced it.
items.requiredFix: Restate as: gradeTurns yields exactly one shapeKey GROUP graded 'held up' (with every eligible window in it carrying the grade), and a build citing any window of that group renders exactly one row. Pick the counted unit in every criterion that says 'yields N'.

items.defect: Requirement 15 makes validate compare the sidecar's `week` field-wise against 'the items week', but validate has no week logic at all: runValidate's signature is `{ cwd, argv, io }` (validate.mjs:141) with no injectable `now`, and the fallback rule the requirement relies on lives in build.mjs's module-private `normalizeWeek` (build.mjs:211-221), which is not exported. An implementer must duplicate normalizeWeek into validate.mjs (silent-drift risk against build's copy) or import lib/build.mjs from lib/validate.mjs, and the documented items-file-without-`week` case becomes wall-clock dependent and untestable.
items.requiredFix: Move `normalizeWeek` into a shared pure module (lib/resolve-week.mjs already exists and both files import from it) and export it, add lib/resolve-week.mjs to filesTouched, and add a `now = new Date()` parameter to runValidate so the fallback-week branch is injectable and its abort is testable.

items.defect: sharesRun's adaptive floor is aggressive enough to make lane authoring impractical, and the phase does not measure it. With n = min(8, max(3, ceil(0.6 * w))), a 5-word technique name is rejected if ANY 3 consecutive words of it occur anywhere in the week's prompt corpus — a corpus of up to MAX_TURNS=400 windows per session across every featured session, each up to MAX_PROMPT_LEN=4000 characters. Common English trigrams ('the failing test', 'before we touch', 'one at a time') will collide constantly, so the honest short names the spec's own plainTerms asks for ('Claude's only job is to name the technique in plain words') are the ones most likely to abort the build. The acceptance criterion 'a 6-word genuine paraphrase passes' is satisfiable only because the test fixture owns the corpus.
items.requiredFix: Either raise the floor (n = max(5, ...)) and keep the whole-string containment rule as the short-string guard, or keep n=3 and add an acceptance criterion measuring the false-positive rate: over a realistic multi-session fixture corpus, assert that a set of ~10 hand-written honest technique names all pass. Add the resulting posture to the risks list so the abort is expected rather than discovered at exit 2.

items.defect: Blocker (TAXONOMY-COLLISION): 'Phase 3 does not render a single mined reversal, so it cannot close #52 item 5.'
items.why: Requirement 3 does add a real engine-sourced render path ('Every reversal string on a discovered handoff becomes a forward row with origin handoff-reversal and disposition ruled out, built by build from discoverHandoffs' own output, INDEPENDENT of whether any authored item cites it'), and criterion REVERSALS RENDER is genuinely end-to-end. What the revision never states is the TRIGGER for the band as a whole, and both readings are contradicted elsewhere in the spec. Reading (a): the band is gated on lane presence (cross-cutting: 'A lane is PRESENT iff Array.isArray(x) && x.length > 0'; req 20 mandates a conditional spread keyed on that; req 15 keys every abort on '`forward` is present'). Under (a) a week whose handoffs record reversals but where the model authored no forward item at all still renders nothing - the same status-quo failure the objection measured, only with the dependency moved from 'an item citing the reversal' to 'any authored item at all', and README.md:12's promise still reaching no output by engine action. Reading (b): reversals render whenever discoverHandoffs yields them, which contradicts cross-cutting Layer 1 ('absent the new keys ... every emitted byte is identical to the pre-change build') and phase-3 criteria 2 (EMPTY LANE IS ABSENT) and 3 (ARCHIVE BYTES) for any corpus whose handoffs contain reversal lines. Neither acceptance criterion disambiguates: criterion REVERSALS RENDER says only 'with NO authored forward item CITING it', which reading (a) satisfies by putting an unrelated forward item in the fixture; and the Phase-2 golden harness points config.repos at a throwaway in-test repo with no .claude/handoffs, so byte-identity holds under both readings. The same ambiguity hits criterion HANDOFF NEXT-STEPS REACH THE BAND ('a handoff ... produces a forward row'): engine-produced, or authored?
items.requiredFix: State the trigger literally in requirement 3: either (i) mined reversal/next-step rows render whenever discoverHandoffs yields them for the week, independent of the items file's `forward` key - in which case add a NAMED exception to cross-cutting Layer 1 and rewrite criteria 2 and 3 to hold 'for a corpus with no handoff-sourced rows', and add a criterion asserting a build with NO `forward` key at all still renders the reversal band; or (ii) the band is gated on lane presence - in which case say so, and say plainly in the PR body and the #52 cross-link that item 5 is closed only for weeks in which the model authored a forward lane. Also state which of the two applies to handoff next-steps.

items.defect: The cross-week carry is unimplementable as specified: there is no join between a carried ref and the row's renderable content. Req 8 strips `ref` from every forward row before emit AND before writeArchive, and fixes the carry file's shape as honestweek.forward-index.json: { week, entries: [{ ref, disposition, dispositionAsOf }] } - no text, no origin, no repo. The archive snapshot (archive.mjs:51-52 serializes the model wholesale) has the text but, by req 8, no ref. So in week 2 build holds a ref with no text and a text with no ref. Yet criterion CROSS-WEEK CARRY requires "a week-1 'not started' ref renders 'deferred' in week 2 with its originating week shown", and req 12 requires carried entries to be re-run through the display-repo check, the configured-private-term check, the P5 noun check and the P3 copy gate - all of which operate on TEXT the spec never says where to get. Week 2's own re-derivation cannot supply it: build re-derives only week 2's session logs, and a 'deferred' idea is by definition one with no signal this week. Req 10's 'tolerate snapshots' does not close it, because the snapshot rows carry no matching key. This is the cost of the fix that closed the ref/archive blocker, and it silently disables the feature rather than contradicting an artifact rule.
items.requiredFix: Give the carry index the full renderable payload it needs and say so: entries: [{ ref, text, origin, disposition, dispositionAsOf, firstSeenWeek, repo? }] (it is gitignored local state, so prose is permitted there under Layer 0), and state that week N renders a carried row FROM THE INDEX, never from the snapshot. Add an acceptance criterion asserting week 2's deferred row's rendered text is byte-equal to week 1's rendered text and that its shown originating week is week 1's start.

items.defect: Rendering mined reversals directly opens a NEW verbatim-prose publish channel with none of the gates the rest of the spec insists on. Req 3 justifies it as 'already redacted and bounded at handoffs.mjs:34/144, exactly like claims[] - publishable structure, not a raw dump'. That analogy is false as measured: nothing in lib/emit or lib/site reads handoffs, claims or reversals (grep returns nothing), and honestweek.draft.json is read only by discover.mjs, harvest.mjs and init.mjs - so handoff prose has NEVER reached a rendered artifact. Under req 3 it now reaches report.md, digest.md and report.html verbatim (280-char truncated), bypassing: SKILL rule 1 distillation, validate entirely (validate.mjs:152-166 reads only config + items, and a mined row is not in the items file), validate.mjs:114-120's display-repo naming rule, the P5 unconfigured-noun check and the P3 copy gate (req 15 scopes both to authored `forward` prose), and checkVoice (build.mjs:297-301 scans { items, content, projects }; req 15's 'thread forward prose into checkVoice' does not say mined rows are included). The exposure is wider than 'a reversal section': handoffs.mjs:88 fires on `(inReversalSection && isBullet) || REVERSAL_LINE_RE.test(line)`, and REVERSAL_LINE_RE (/\b(revers|reverted|rolled back|don'?t resurrect|corrected)\b/i) matches ANY line anywhere in the file - so an ordinary handoff line such as 'corrected the invoice for <client> before the call' is published. Handoffs are assistant-drafted free prose (the spec itself argues this in req 4), i.e. exactly the surface P1-P5 were written to keep out of rendered output. No acceptance criterion covers it: the NEGATIVE CONTROL fixture places its unconfigured noun in an idea TURN only.
items.requiredFix: Subject every engine-sourced forward row's text to the same gates as authored lane prose before it can render: the P5 harvestNouns/excludeSet check, the configured-private-term check, the display-repo naming check, and checkVoice (as its own keyed collection), aborting exit 2 under the same rules. Narrow the source: only lines from a REVERSAL_HEADING_RE section may become a rendered row (the free-floating REVERSAL_LINE_RE branch stays draft-only). Add a negative-control criterion: an unconfigured private noun inside a handoff reversal line appears in NO rendered artifact and in NO archive snapshot. Correct req 3's rationale sentence, which currently asserts a false equivalence with claims[].

items.defect: Acceptance criterion NO REF ANYWHERE PUBLISHED is unsatisfiable as written alongside req 2. It demands 'no 8-hex value that is not a git-verified shortSha appears in report.md, digest.md, post.md, changelog.md, report.html, goals.html, the site bundle, or the archive snapshot'. But req 2 keeps `receipt: { sessionId, turn }` on every forward row (req 5: 'the receipt is DISPLAY metadata only'), only `ref` is stripped (req 8), and the archive snapshot is the model verbatim (archive.mjs:51-52). receipt.sessionId IS an 8-hex value: claude-adapter.mjs shortId() returns firstSeg.toLowerCase().slice(0,8) of a UUID, and the committed fixtures yield exactly 'aaaaaaaa', 'bbbbbbbb', etc. The same scan also trips on existing WORK items, whose session receipts render through _shared.mjs:47 receiptPointer as a backticked 8-hex sessionId in real (non-fixture) corpora.
items.requiredFix: Rewrite the criterion to assert what the protection actually is: the specific ref values computed by that build (read from honestweek.forward-index.json) appear in no rendered artifact and in no archive snapshot, and honestweek.forward-index.json is gitignored after `init` alone. If the generic 8-hex scan is kept, exempt receipt.sessionId explicitly - or state that receipts are stripped from forward rows before emit and writeArchive too, since req 24 says forward rows render no receipt anyway.

items.defect: The carry index's specified shape cannot support the rules built on it. Req 8 fixes it as a single-week file ({ week: {start,end}, entries: [...] }) written 'beside the snapshot', while req 9's zombie rule ranges over 'ANY prior carry-index entry' and criterion CROSS-WEEK CARRY requires a deferred row to show 'its originating week'. If week N overwrites the file with week N's entries, week 3 cannot see a ref that reached 'picked up' in week 1, and originating-week provenance is lost after one hop; if it accumulates, the top-level `week` field, the merge rule, and any pruning/retention bound are unspecified. Its LOCATION is also ambiguous: 'written by build beside the snapshot' points at config.output.archiveDir, while 'added to init's and the repo's .gitignore alongside the Phase-1 sidecars' and criterion 4's read point at the project root - a test and a reader need one answer. Related unstated consequence: because the index is written only on the archive path (build.mjs:422 gates on config.output.archive && redactedForArchive, default false at config.mjs:216, null in the site branch), the zombie rule is inert by default, which req 13 states for 'deferred' but not for the zombie rule.
items.requiredFix: State whether the index accumulates across weeks and, if so, its merge key, retention bound and pruning rule; carry a per-entry firstSeenWeek; fix its path literally (repo root vs archiveDir) and match criterion 4 and the init test to it; and add one sentence to req 13 noting the zombie rule, like 'deferred', is archive-gated and therefore off by default.

items.defect: Engine-generated forward rows have no specified `id` or `ref` derivation, and the obvious derivation violates the spec's own pattern. Req 2 makes `id` REQUIRED and matching /^forward-[a-z0-9-]+$/ and unique; req 5 aborts exit 2 when `ref` is absent; criterion ABORTS makes 'a malformed/duplicate id' an exit-2. But mined reversal rows (req 3) are built by build, not authored, so build must mint both - and the only defined generator, Phase 1's refFor(sessionId, turnIndex, origin, redactedText), is session/turn-shaped and has no meaning for a handoff record whose receipt is { handoffId }. The natural id source is handoffs.mjs:60-63 handoffId(), which returns a timestamp token such as '20260626T170459Z' (uppercase T and Z) or 'handoff-<8hex>' - the first fails /^forward-[a-z0-9-]+$/ outright and would trip build's own malformed-id abort. Determinism matters here beyond convenience: these ids and refs must be stable for the golden byte-identity and archive criteria.
items.requiredFix: Define, in req 2 or 3, the deterministic id and ref derivation for handoff-sourced rows (e.g. ref = shortHash(handoffId + '|' + origin + '|' + normalizePhrase(text)); id = 'forward-' + lowercased handoffId with non-[a-z0-9-] characters mapped to '-', plus a stable per-handoff ordinal for uniqueness), and add it to the disposeForward/lanes.mjs test plan.

items.defect: No specified behavior when the resolveCommit path throws. Req 6 enumerates 'a nominated-but-unresolved SHA', a log/show/rev-parse SHA and a wrong-author SHA as yielding 'not started', but lib/git.mjs lookupCommit (:71-74) THROWS when repoPath is not a usable git repository - a routine state for a configured repo whose path has moved. The forward gate is deliberately placed OUTSIDE the emit try/catch (req 15), so an uncaught throw there would surface as an unhandled error rather than the specified exit-2-or-'not started'.
items.requiredFix: Add one clause to req 6: a resolveCommit that throws is treated exactly like a non-resolving SHA (disposition 'not started'), never as an abort or an uncaught error, and cover it in the lanes.mjs table-driven test.

items.defect: Stale code reference: req 24 and criterion CONTRACT STRINGS SCOPED cite 'test/skill.test.mjs:179' as the pre-existing presence check. That file is 86 lines long; the assertion (/receipt on every item|No item ships without/i) is at test/skill.test.mjs:46. Every other line reference I checked in this phase is accurate (build.mjs:47-70/:81/:119/:261/:352-366/:386/:405/:422, archive.mjs:17/:26/:51-56, handoffs.mjs:34/:137/:144, config.mjs:216, goals.mjs:493, page.mjs:160/:168/:391, report.mjs:46, digest.mjs:48, validate.mjs:114-127, docs.test.mjs:62-69/:74/:101-103/:122, build.test.mjs:94).
items.requiredFix: Change the citation to test/skill.test.mjs:46.

items.defect: Phase 3 resolves every forward row by `ref` ("aborts exit 2 when `ref` is absent or matches no idea / next-step / reversal record"), and keys the carry index and the zombie rule on `ref`. Phase 1 mints refs ONLY for transcript-mined prompts and ideas: refFor(sessionId, turnIndex, origin, redactedText). Handoff next-steps (Phase 1 req 25) and reversals (existing, handoffs.mjs:144) are emitted as bare redacted strings with no identity of any kind, and refFor's signature cannot produce one for them (a handoff has no sessionId and no turnIndex). So the two origins that actually deliver issue #52 items 4 and 5 ('handoff-next-step', 'handoff-reversal') have no resolvable key, cannot be carried across weeks, and cannot be suppressed by the zombie rule. Verified in the repo: discoverHandoffs pushes `reversals: reversals.map(t => red.redact(t))` and nothing else.
items.requiredFix: Phase 1 must mint a stable per-line ref for handoff-sourced lines. Add `refForHandoffLine(handoffId, lineIndex, origin, redactedText)` to lib/lanes.mjs and have discoverHandoffs emit NEW sibling arrays (e.g. nextStepRefs/reversalRefs, or nextSteps/reversals as parallel `{ref,text}` lists under new key names). It must be a sibling, not a reshape of `reversals`, because Phase 1's own DRAFT SUPERSET criterion requires handoffs[].reversals to deepEqual its pre-change value. The ref input must include handoffId and line index, not text alone, since two handoffs can carry byte-identical reversal lines after 280-char truncation. Phase 3 then states which function produces the ref for each of its four origins.

items.defect: The cross-week carry has no path from a week-1 record to a rendered week-2 row. Phase 3 defines honestweek.forward-index.json entries as `{ ref, disposition, dispositionAsOf }` (no text, no origin, no id), and simultaneously strips `ref` from every archive snapshot. So the only store holding the carried row's prose (the week-1 snapshot) has no join key, and the only store holding the join key has no prose. Yet Phase 3 requires week 2 to RENDER the carried row ('a week-1 not-started ref renders deferred in week 2 with its originating week shown') and to re-run that row's TEXT through the display-repo check, the configured-private-term check, the P5 noun check and the P3 copy gate. The spec mandates text-based re-gating of an entity it defines as text-free.
items.requiredFix: Make honestweek.forward-index.json self-contained local state: entries carry `{ ref, id, text, origin, receipt, disposition, dispositionAsOf, firstSeenWeek }`. That satisfies the carry render, the re-gating branch, and P6's rule that matching keys stay out of published surfaces, without putting refs back into the snapshot. Update Phase 3's index shape, its carry acceptance criterion, and the archive test plan accordingly.

items.defect: Phase 1's MAX_TURNS acceptance criterion is internally contradictory, and Phase 2's 'held up' fail-closed rule depends on which reading wins. Phase 1 requires 'A synthetic session with 500 turns yields turns.length === 400, entry.truncatedAtTurn === 400, AND every past-cap window present as `{index, stub:true, complete:false}` (asserted by key set, not by absence)'. Those cannot both hold: 400 non-stub windows plus 100 stubs is length 500. Phase 2 then writes its truncation guard against the stub reading ('If ANY window in the corpus carrying that shapeKey is a stub'), which is additionally vacuous because Phase 1's stub record carries no shapeKey field at all ('no other fields'). The only operative guard left is `truncatedAtTurn !== null`.
items.requiredFix: Pick one representation in Phase 1 and propagate it. Recommended: turns[] holds up to MAX_TURNS non-stub windows PLUS stubs for every clipped window (so turns.length === 500 and the count of non-stub windows === 400), with the criterion reworded to assert both numbers. Then delete Phase 2's vacuous 'carrying that shapeKey is a stub' clause and restate the fail-closed rule as: the group does not grade 'held up' if any session contributing a window with that shapeKey has truncatedAtTurn !== null, or if any stub exists in such a session.

items.defect: Where the lane keys attach relative to `redactor.deepRedact` is never stated, and the two phases need opposite answers. Phase 2 says attach 'into the markdown emit call site (build.mjs:405)'. Verified: build.mjs:405 is `redactedForArchive = redactor.deepRedact(model)` and :406 is `emit(redactedForArchive, ...)`. Attaching to the object at/after :405 puts technique and forward prose into the emitted file AND into the archive snapshot without ever passing the deepRedact backstop that every other authored string gets, while page mode (buildPageModel at :385, redacted at :386) does redact it. That is a mode-dependent redaction hole. Attaching before deepRedact instead is the safe reading but reads as 'inside the model', which Phase 2 forbids. Phase 3 then hard-requires the lane to BE in the snapshot (dispositionAsOf survives into it, forwardOpen counts it, 'no ref in the written bytes'), which forces the pre-redaction attachment.
items.requiredFix: State the rule once, in Phase 2, and have Phase 3 inherit it: lanes attach to the model object AFTER assembleReportModel returns and BEFORE redactor.deepRedact, in both the page branch and the markdown branch, never inside assembleReportModel and never into the site path. Add an acceptance criterion that a configured redaction term placed inside a technique text and a forward text is scrubbed in digest, report, page AND the archive snapshot.

items.defect: Phase 2's fail-closed sidecar check reads a field Phase 1 is never required to write. Phase 2 requires validate to compare honestweek.prompts.json's `week` to the items week FIELD-WISE and exit 2 on mismatch. The `{ generatedAt, week:{start,end}, prompts:[...], ideas:[...] }` envelope appears only in cross-cutting.json (P2). Phase 1's requirement 22 says only 'write honestweek.prompts.json sourced from the sink', its sink rows are `{ref,sessionId,turn,text}` / `{ref,sessionId,turn,origin,cue,text}`, and NO Phase 1 acceptance criterion asserts the file's top-level shape (the SIDECAR criterion asserts creation, gitignore ordering and the MAX_PROMPT_LEN cap only). An implementer working from phase-1.json alone ships a sidecar with no `week`, and Phase 2's stale-corpus abort silently degrades to always-abort or never-abort.
items.requiredFix: Move the sidecar envelope into a Phase 1 REQUIREMENT and add a Phase 1 acceptance criterion asserting the exact top-level shape, including `week.start`/`week.end` equal to the discover run's week and `generatedAt`. Phase 2's week-comparison criterion then has something to assert against.

items.defect: Both lanes need to resolve a commit 'in the session's repo', but Phase 1 emits no repo path and no phase defines resolveCommit's signature. Verified: adaptOneSession emits `repo: repo.label` (a label string; privateEntry emits null) and carries no cwd or resolvedPath, while lib/git.mjs's verifyItems does its own `repoByLabel` map and then `lookupCommit(repoPath, sha, authorEmails)`. Phase 2 injects `resolveCommit` into gradeTurns and Phase 3 injects `resolveCommit` into disposeForward, each describing the same three-part rule (git-commit-sourced SHA, resolves, authored) in prose, with no shared signature and no statement that the session's repo is a LABEL requiring a config.repos lookup. Two phases will implement the same predicate twice and can diverge on the display-role refusal.
items.requiredFix: Phase 2 defines `resolveCommit(sha, repoLabel) -> { resolved, byAuthor }` once, built from config.repos label lookup plus lookupCommit, refusing display-role repos before any git invocation, and names entry.repo as the label it is keyed by. Phase 3 states that disposeForward takes the SAME injected function and does not restate the rule.

items.defect: Phase 3's mined-reversal rows are the first path in the codebase from handoff prose to a rendered artifact, and they bypass every check the lane spec builds. Verified: grep across lib/emit and lib/site finds no reader of handoffs[].claims or .reversals, so no handoff prose is published today; and validate.mjs reads only config + items (existsSync/readFileSync on itemsPath alone). Phase 3 has build inject a forward row for every reversal string INDEPENDENT of any authored item, so those rows never appear in honestweek.items.json, are never seen by validate rules 11-14 (copy gate, display-repo check, configured-private-term check, P5 noun check), and have no authored `forward-*` id, which Phase 3 itself mandates as the voice-fence ref-namespacing mechanism. Phase 3 justifies this as 'already redacted and bounded, exactly like claims[]', but claims[] are a distillation INPUT, not published output.
items.requiredFix: Name the injected-row branch explicitly: state that build mints deterministic ids for mined reversal rows (e.g. `forward-rev-<handoffId>-<n>`), and that build re-runs the display-repo check, the configured-private-term check and the P5 noun check over mined reversal text at build time (the copy gate is moot for text that was never authored). Add an acceptance criterion that a configured private term and an unconfigured coined noun inside a reversal line are caught on the mined path, not only the authored path.

items.defect: Phase 3 makes build trust a model-writable local JSON for dispositions, which is exactly what Phase 2 and cross-cutting P6 forbid. P6's own heading is 'build trusts NO model-writable file', and Phase 2's blocker-level correction removes honestweek.draft.json from build's inputs on the grounds that 'the draft is a gitignored local JSON the same model that authors the items file can write'. honestweek.forward-index.json is the same class of file: gitignored, local, writable by the same model, and Phase 3 has build read dispositions and terminal states straight out of it to mint 'deferred' and to suppress rows via the zombie rule. The blast radius is smaller than the draft's (both effects under-claim rather than over-claim), but the stated invariant is absolute and is now false.
items.requiredFix: Either state the exception explicitly in P6 and in SKILL.md ('the carry index is engine-written local state; a tampered index can only suppress or defer a row, never mint a verified claim'), or re-derive the carry state from the archive snapshots plus this week's corpus so no new trusted file is introduced. Do not leave the absolute wording standing beside the exception.

items.defect: The zombie rule needs cumulative history but the carry index is defined as single-week and overwritten. Phase 3 requires 'a ref that reached picked up or ruled out in ANY prior carry-index entry is never re-surfaced in a later week', while defining the file as `{ week: {start,end}, entries: [...] }` written beside the snapshot on each build. Once a ref is ruled out in week 1 it is (correctly) not carried into week 2, so it is absent from week 2's index, so by week 3 the terminal state is forgotten and the idea resurrects. Phase 3's acceptance criterion only tests two weeks, so the corpus reads green over the defect.
items.requiredFix: Make the index cumulative (retain terminal entries with `firstSeenWeek` and `closedInWeek`, pruning never or on an explicit bound) or write one index file per week beside each snapshot and read all of them. Extend the acceptance criterion to three weeks: ruled out in week 1, absent from week 2, still suppressed in week 3.

items.defect: The three rendered contract strings are re-authored by two phases with different required wordings and no stated combined matrix. Phase 2 requires digest.mjs:25 and the page foot div to swap to 'a scoped variant naming the transcript-derived bands' when a lane band is present, and pins that wording with an acceptance criterion. Phase 3 then requires the same foot div (plus README.md:285 and SKILL.md:43) to be 'scoped to WORK items with the forward band named as the carried-forward exception', asserted by regex. Phase 3 therefore rewrites the exact literal Phase 2's test pins, and neither phase enumerates the four presence cases (neither band / Lane A only / Lane B only / both).
items.requiredFix: Phase 2 defines the contract string as a single function of `{ hasTechniques, hasForward }` covering all four cases (the Lane B cases render the Lane-A-only text until Phase 3 fills them in), and writes its acceptance criterion parametrically over that function. Phase 3 only supplies the two Lane B branches. The golden harness pins the neither-band case in both phases.

items.defect: `opensWithCorrection` is in Phase 1's fixed turn key set but no requirement defines it, and no phase consumes it by name. Phase 2's correctionObserved tri-state is defined in terms of 'the next window opens with a correction', which is presumably this field, but the link is never written down.
items.requiredFix: Define opensWithCorrection in Phase 1 as isCorrectionTurn(window instruction text) and state in Phase 2 that correctionObserved is derived from the NEXT window's opensWithCorrection.

items.defect: An idea mined from an assistant text block before the first turn boundary has no window. Phase 1 requires records emitted before the first boundary to carry `turn: null` and creates no synthetic window 0, but the idea record shape is `{ turn, ref, origin, cue }` with no null case stated. Phase 3's 'picked up' rule reads 'the entry's own turn window has a commitShas SHA', which has no referent when turn is null.
items.requiredFix: Phase 1 states that an idea cue firing before the first boundary produces NO idea record (matching the tool-attribution skip), or emits turn: null explicitly; Phase 3 states that a null-turn forward row is always 'not started'.

items.defect: Every phase's acceptance rests on the hermetic golden harness, but its git determinism is under-specified. Phase 1 requires 'config.repos at an in-test throwaway git repo' plus a fixed `now` and a pinned CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Commit SHAs and dates in a freshly created repo vary per run unless author/committer name, email and BOTH date env vars are pinned, and page/site modes render git-derived numbers and shortShas.
items.requiredFix: Phase 1 states that the throwaway repo is created with GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE all pinned, so SHAs are reproducible. The 'identical bytes on two consecutive runs' criterion should be strengthened to 'identical bytes from two independently constructed repos'.

items.defect: When both lane keys are present, Phase 2's build calls adaptSessions for grading and Phase 3's build calls it again for forward resolution, plus discoverHandoffs. No phase says the re-derivation is computed once and shared, so a both-lanes build pays two full transcript scans of the same corpus with two redactor instances.
items.requiredFix: Phase 2 specifies a single lazily-computed re-derivation (`ensureLaneCorpus()`) memoized for the build, and Phase 3 consumes it rather than calling adaptSessions itself.

items.defect: Phase 3 adds `forwardOpen` to archive.mjs's index entry without saying whether it is conditional on lane presence. Verified: writeArchive pushes a fixed-shape index entry, so an unconditional field changes archive/index.json bytes for every archive-enabled user with no forward band. Phase 3's ARCHIVE BYTES criterion pins the snapshot only, so nothing catches it.
items.requiredFix: State that forwardOpen is added under the same conditional-spread presence rule as the model key, and extend the ARCHIVE BYTES criterion to cover index.json.

items.defect: SKILL.md's rule count is updated once but amended twice. Phase 2 adds rule 7 and requires test/skill.test.mjs's name and count to be updated in the same commit. Phase 3 adds 'a contract clause covering origin honesty, the closedBy receipt rule and the never-copy rule' without saying it is rule 8 or that the count assertion must move again.
items.requiredFix: Phase 3 names its addition as SKILL.md rule 8 and repeats the update-the-count-and-title instruction.

items.defect: Phase 3 promises mined reversals render "INDEPENDENT of whether any authored item cites it" (phase-3.json req 3), but cross-cutting.json gates the whole reversal path on lane presence and phase-3.json's own acceptance criterion says an items file carrying `"forward": []` must be byte-identical to one omitting the key with "no gate fired" — so in the normal case (a week where the distilling model authors no forward item) handoff reversals still render nothing, leaving README.md:12's "the dead ends you ruled out" and issue #52 item 5's acceptance unmet, which is the exact residual failure this phase claims to have fixed.
items.requiredFix: Split lane PRESENCE into two triggers and say so once: authored-item presence gates the copy/noun/ref gates, but the engine-sourced forward rows (handoff reversals and handoff next-steps) render whenever discoverHandoffs yields them, regardless of the `forward` key. Then rewrite the EMPTY-LANE-IS-ABSENT criterion to hold only for a week whose handoffs carry zero reversals and zero next-steps, and add an acceptance test with an items file that has NO forward key at all plus a reversal-bearing handoff, asserting the row renders.

items.defect: README.md:283-285 names "A receipt on every line" as one of honestweek's two non-negotiable promises, and AGENTS.md:40 restates it as invariant 1; phase-3.json (req 15, Docs) closes the gap by REWORDING that promise to work items rather than satisfying it, even though every lane row already holds a resolvable source pointer (Lane A carries { sessionId, turn }; forward rows carry { sessionId, turn } or { handoffId }) that the plan demotes to "DISPLAY metadata only" and never renders.
items.requiredFix: Require every lane row to RENDER its non-git receipt (the 8-hex session id + turn index, or the handoff id) in all three modes, styled distinctly from a git SHA so it cannot be read as a commit. Then the README/SKILL scoping shrinks from "receipt on every line applies only to work items" to the far weaker and true "a git receipt on every work line; a transcript receipt on every lane line", and the launch invariant survives intact instead of being narrowed.

items.defect: AGENTS.md is the conventions file the Codex sessions implementing these three PRs will read as their operative constraint set, yet it appears in no phase's `filesTouched`, while the plan makes two of its six invariants false — invariant 1 ("An item reaching a renderer without a receipt is a build error", AGENTS.md:40-41) and invariant 6 ("New output is additive. Absent its new inputs, existing output stays byte-identical", AGENTS.md:49-50, contradicted by Phase 1's handoffs.mjs:137 emptiness-guard change, which additivityStrategy itself labels "a genuine, intended behaviour delta on existing repos" requiring no new input).
items.requiredFix: Add AGENTS.md to Phase 1's and Phase 3's filesTouched: Phase 1 amends invariant 6 to name the handoff next-steps delta as the one sanctioned exception (or restates additivity per-layer as cross-cutting.json already does); Phase 3 amends invariant 1 with whatever receipt scoping is settled. Add an acceptance criterion extending test/docs.test.mjs's README/SKILL non-contradiction assertion to cover AGENTS.md's invariant list, so the three cannot drift again.

items.defect: phase-2.json req 14 correctly refuses to let the proxy borrow the construct's name at the FIELD level (`repeatedOpenings`, not `techniqueRecurrence`) but then ships rendered labels that do exactly that: TECHNIQUE_GRADES = ['worked first time','held up','needed correction'] asserts an outcome, while what is measured is "no correction observed in the next window, plus a typed test flip or a verified commit in that window" — against AGENTS.md:44-45 invariant 3 ("Never assert a motive, cause, or outcome the log does not contain") and README.md:286's under-claim promise, with only an adjacent GRADE_DEFINITIONS line standing between the label and the reader.
items.requiredFix: Apply the same renaming discipline to the vocabulary as to the field: name the grades after what was measured, not after the inferred outcome (e.g. 'no correction, test flipped', 'recurred uncorrected', 'corrected then landed'), or at minimum add an acceptance criterion asserting each rendered grade label is accompanied inline — not merely elsewhere in the section — by its GRADE_DEFINITIONS clause. Decide this before Phase 2 lands; a published grade vocabulary is expensive to rename later.

items.defect: Every lane failure is whole-build fatal with no one-command off-ramp: it is Sunday night, the operator's scheduled run builds a week whose ~/.claude session logs were pruned (or runs on a second machine, or after `git clean -xfd`), the lane gate hits 'session-log root yields ZERO files', build exits 2 and writes nothing, so the operator loses the entire work report because of an optional bonus band, and the only documented recovery is to hand-open honestweek.items.json and delete two top-level keys, which is exactly the remember-to-do-it manual step that gets dropped. The plan names this cost in phase-2 risks and mitigates it with a README sentence ('must be in the README, not discovered at exit 2'), but a README is not an off-ramp and there is no `--no-lanes` flag anywhere in the three phases.
items.requiredFix: Split the lane gate's two failure classes. A corpus-absent or unresolvable-record condition should DROP the lane loudly (stderr names the band, the reason, and the row count dropped) and still emit the work report, since dropping an uncheckable row is the under-claim direction the spec already takes for ungraded windows; reserve exit 2 for a positive dishonesty hit (copy gate, display-repo, strictLaneNouns). If abort is kept, add an explicit `--no-lanes` flag to build and validate and require every lane abort message to name it verbatim, so the remedy is one command rather than a JSON edit.

items.defect: The only document the authoring model reads at runtime does not carry the predicate that fatally gates its output: the SKILL.md rule 7 text mandated in phase-2 tells the model 'a window with no measured outcome... is DROPPED' but never states what makes a window ineligible (stub, complete === false, kind === 'command', shapeKey === null) or what mints a grade (correctionObserved === 'no' plus a typed testRunFlip or a git-resolved authored commit), so the model authors a technique, build re-derives, the row is ungraded, and the whole build exits 2 with 'no measured outcome' - and the operator's only lever is to tell Claude to guess again, at one extra full transcript scan per attempt. The `committed` disjunct is genuinely unknowable from the draft (it needs git resolution plus authorship), so even a careful model cannot avoid this by reading its own input.
items.requiredFix: Require SKILL.md's rule 7 / '### Technique item shape' block to state the eligibility predicate and name the draft turn fields that carry it (stub, complete, kind, shapeKey, correctionObserved, testSignals, commitShas), plus an explicit instruction to omit a technique whose only evidence is an unverified commit SHA. Same for phase 3's '### Forward item shape': state that `ref` must be copied verbatim from a draft ideas[] record. Optionally add a read-only `honestweek build --explain-lanes` that prints the gradeable window list so authoring is informed rather than a retry loop.

items.defect: The P5 unconfigured-noun check is specified to fire on any capitalized token outside excludeSet, and the plan itself concedes 'Claude', 'Node' and 'Windows' 'would fire constantly' - so every weekly validate and every lane build prints per-item warning lines the operator cannot clear and should not act on (technique names in plain words will routinely contain 'Claude'), which trains them to stop reading stderr; that is the same channel phase 3 adds the corrupt-snapshot warning to precisely so 'an idea does not vanish with no diagnostic', and the same channel carries issue #49's zero-session-logs warning. The plan chose warning-over-abort to avoid a false-positive machine but did nothing to reduce the false positives.
items.requiredFix: Seed the exported excludeSet with the ambient toolchain vocabulary the corpus guarantees will appear (Claude, Node, Windows, Git, Bash, Edit, Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Task, plus the configured repo labels), and print the residual noun check as a COUNT only by default - matching the counts-only discipline the plan already cites from harvest.mjs:149-153 - with per-id detail behind an explicit flag or under strictLaneNouns. Add an acceptance criterion that a lane build over the fixture corpus emits zero noun warnings, so the channel stays meaningful for the diagnostics phase 3 depends on.

items.defect: The lane gate runs in every mode but only digest, report and page render a lane band, so an operator whose output.mode is `post` - the build-in-public update, and the most natural home for 'prompts that worked' - pays every lane cost (an extra transcript scan, the copy gate, a possible exit 2 that writes nothing) and gets zero rendered output, with nothing at authoring time or config time telling them their mode cannot show the band. The plan explicitly reasons about site mode's gate-without-render case and rewrote its acceptance criterion for it, but post and changelog are left unaddressed in both directions.
items.requiredFix: Decide post and changelog explicitly in the spec rather than by omission. Either add a lane section to post.mjs and changelog.mjs (built on laneBadge, never through allItems), or state that lanes are unrendered there and require build to print a single stdout line when lane keys are present in a non-rendering mode ('techniques/forward present but output.mode `post` renders no lane band; N rows ignored'), with an acceptance criterion pinning that line.

items.defect: Phase 2 rule 10 / P5 introduce a new settings key `config.redaction.strictLaneNouns` read by validate and build, but lib/config.mjs is the declared owner of the config schema and rebuilds `redaction` as a three-key whitelist (config.mjs:156-160 -> `{codenames, names, terms}`, returned at :245), so the key is silently dropped at load and the flag is unreachable; lib/config.mjs appears in no phase's filesTouched, and README's config-reference table (the declared read surface for every config key) gains no row for it.
items.requiredFix: Add lib/config.mjs to Phase 2 filesTouched and require an explicit normalization+validation branch (`strictLaneNouns` boolean, default false, fail-loud on a non-boolean, mirroring the voice.denyMeta pattern at config.mjs:230-238), add a README config-table row and a test/config.test.mjs assertion that the key survives loadConfig. Otherwise the Phase 2 acceptance criterion 'the same input with strictLaneNouns true exits 2' cannot pass through the real loader.

items.defect: AGENTS.md is the constitution Codex reads ('Read this before changing anything', invariants 'that must not break'), yet it appears in no phase's filesTouched while Phases 1 and 3 deliberately narrow two of its six invariants: invariant 1 ('a receipt on every line ... an item reaching a renderer without a receipt is a build error') is contradicted by Phase 3's forward band, which requirement 24 concedes 'render[s] with neither a badge nor a receipt', and invariant 6 ('absent its new inputs, existing output stays byte-identical') is contradicted by cross-cutting Layer 2/2b, which knowingly changes honestweek.draft.json bytes for existing users via redact-before-truncate and the handoffs.mjs:137 guard.
items.requiredFix: Add AGENTS.md to Phase 1's and Phase 3's filesTouched with the same scoping edits already mandated for README.md:285 / SKILL.md:43 / the page.mjs foot div: scope invariant 1 to work items and name the carried-forward band as the declared exception, and restate invariant 6 with cross-cutting's Layer 0 split (rendered artifacts strictly byte-identical; local-state artifacts additive-superset). An implementer reading only AGENTS.md today must either block Phase 1 or break a stated invariant.

items.defect: SKILL.md's orchestrator flow is the model's operating contract, and no phase updates step 2 (discover, 'output: honestweek.draft.json') or step 3 (DISTIL, 'input: honestweek.draft.json') to name honestweek.prompts.json — yet Phase 1 P1 strips all free text out of the draft's turns[]/ideas[] (refs, cues and shapeKeys only), so under the docs as they will ship the model has no instructed source from which to author a technique or forward `text`; cross-cutting.json privacyDecision P2 states the intent ('The model reads the sidecar locally to name a technique or an idea') but no phase turns it into a requirement. Searched: phase-1 requirement 24 (docs: Sidecars table, README:83/SKILL.md:25 handoff yield, SKILL.md:25 draft-shape, output.mode enumeration), phase-2 requirement 11 (rule 7 + technique item shape), phase-3 requirement 19 (forward item shape + privacy bullet) — SKILL rule 7 only forbids copying from the sidecar, it never instructs reading it.
items.requiredFix: Add to Phase 2's docs requirement: SKILL.md step 2 gains honestweek.prompts.json as a second discover output (gitignored, verbatim, local-only); step 3 DISTIL gains it as a second input with a one-line rule ('read it to understand what you asked for; name the technique in your own words; never copy a run of words from it'); step 4's validate sentence gains the new abort classes (missing/stale sidecar, lane id/receipt, copy gate). Add an acceptance criterion that test/skill.test.mjs asserts DISTIL's input list names both files.

items.defect: Phase 3 makes `ref` the mandatory matching key for every forward row ('aborts exit 2 when ref is absent or matches no idea / next-step / reversal record'), and the carry index and zombie rule key on it, but no phase defines how a ref is derived for handoff-sourced records: Phase 1's refFor(sessionId, turnIndex, origin, redactedText) is specified only for turn windows and transcript ideas, and Phase 1 requirement 22 adds handoffs.mjs nextSteps[] as bare redacted strings with no ref (measured: handoffs.mjs:143-144 emits claims/reversals as plain objects/strings under a per-handoff `id` from handoffId(name), with no per-line identifier). Searched phase-1 requirements 2/22/23, phase-3 requirements 2/5/8/9 and cross-cutting P6 — the handoff-side ref is never defined, so the model also cannot author a forward item for a next-step.
items.requiredFix: Add a Phase 1 requirement defining refFor over handoff-sourced records explicitly — e.g. refFor(handoffId, lineIndex, origin, redactedText) with the same shortHash — emit it on each nextSteps[] and reversals[] entry in the draft (so the model can cite it), and state the week-to-week stability property the carry index depends on. Add a lanes.test.mjs assertion that a handoff next-step and a handoff reversal from the same handoff get distinct, run-stable refs.

items.defect: The activation condition for engine-generated forward rows is never stated, and two plan rules give opposite answers: phase-3 requirement 3 says every mined reversal renders 'INDEPENDENT of whether any authored item cites it' (this is what closes #52 item 5 and README.md:12's 'the dead ends you ruled out'), while cross-cutting.json additivityStrategy Layer 1 plus phase-3's 'EMPTY LANE IS ABSENT' criterion require byte-identical output whenever the items file's `forward` key is absent or `[]`, under the single presence definition (Array.isArray && length > 0) evaluated over the AUTHORED key. So for the common week where the model authors zero forward items but the handoffs carry reversals, the plan simultaneously requires the reversals to render and requires no bytes to change. Searched phase-3 requirements 1-3 and 13, and cross-cutting Layer 0/Layer 1 — no rule resolves it.
items.requiredFix: State the presence rule for the forward band explicitly in one place: either (a) the band activates on the AUTHORED key only, and the #52-item-5 acceptance criterion is rewritten to require at least one authored forward item present (with the consequence — a zero-authored week publishes no reversals — written down), or (b) presence is (authored rows ∪ engine-derived rows).length > 0, and Layer 1's byte-identity gate is restated as conditional on the fixture week yielding no handoff reversals/next-steps. Add the matching acceptance criterion for whichever branch is chosen.

items.defect: Phase 3's 'NO REF ANYWHERE PUBLISHED' criterion — 'a scan asserts no 8-hex value that is not a git-verified shortSha appears in report.md, digest.md, post.md, changelog.md, report.html, goals.html, the site bundle, or the archive snapshot' — fails against pre-existing, correct behaviour and so cannot pass as written: emit/_shared.mjs receiptPointer() resolves `r.shortSha || r.sha || r.sessionId || r.ref || r.turn`, and a session id is the 8-hex shortId (claude-adapter.mjs:438-444), so any work item whose receipt carries only a sessionId — guaranteed for every private/display one-line entry under SKILL.md contract rule 6 — already renders a non-SHA 8-hex string in every mode. The criterion measures the wrong construct (any 8-hex token) for the thing it wants to guarantee (no lane `ref` reaches a published surface).
items.requiredFix: Rewrite the criterion to assert on the known ref values rather than on 8-hex shape: the test builds a week with a populated forward[], collects the exact ref strings from honestweek.forward-index.json, and asserts each is absent from every rendered artifact and from the archive snapshot; separately assert every forward row object written to the snapshot has no `ref` key. Note in the criterion that 8-hex session ids legitimately appear in work-item receipts.
